# Release Quality Checklist: CLI Queue Sequencer

**Purpose**: Exhaustive release gate requirements quality validation for concurrency, resilience, and cross-platform behaviors.
**Created**: 2026-08-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](specs/001-cli-queue-sequencer/spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Concurrency & Lock Safety (Requirement Completeness & Clarity)

- [X] CHK001 Are the exact OS-native mechanisms for file locking specified for each platform (Windows/Linux/macOS)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013]
- [X] CHK002 Is the behavior specified when two concurrent processes attempt to acquire the lock at the exact same microsecond? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [X] CHK003 Are the performance overhead requirements for lock acquisition explicitly quantified? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]
- [X] CHK004 Does the spec define what happens if the JSON state file write fails mid-flight (e.g., disk full)? [Exception Flow, Gap]
- [X] CHK005 Are requirements consistent between "strict FIFO ordering" and high-contention enqueue bursts? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002]

## Resilience & Crash Recovery (Scenario Coverage)

- [X] CHK006 Are detection mechanisms for stale locks explicitly defined (e.g., checking PID liveness)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
- [X] CHK007 Is the recovery procedure documented if a queue process is forcibly killed (SIGKILL) rather than SIGTERM? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011]
- [X] CHK008 Are requirements defined for state corruption scenarios (e.g., invalid JSON in `.state.json`)? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [X] CHK009 Does the spec define the exact timeout behavior if a stale lock cannot be resolved? [Gap]
- [X] CHK010 Are cleanup requirements specified when a wrapped command orphans child processes? [Coverage, Gap]

## Cross-Platform Consistency

- [X] CHK011 Are differences in signal handling requirements between Unix (process groups) and Windows (console events) documented? [Completeness, Plan §Constitution Check]
- [X] CHK012 Are requirements for temporary directory resolution defined across all supported OS? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [X] CHK013 Are exit code propagation edge cases (e.g., Windows codes > 255) specified? [Coverage, Gap]

## I/O & Signal Forwarding (Clarity & Measurability)

- [X] CHK014 Is "real-time streaming" quantified with specific maximum buffering thresholds? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [X] CHK015 Are requirements specified for commands that read interactively from stdin (e.g., TUI)? [Coverage, Spec §Assumptions]
- [X] CHK016 Does the spec clearly define how queue-internal stderr warnings are distinguished from the wrapped command's stderr? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-015]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
